To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
warm dark matter haloes are less massive and have fewer low mass progenitor haloes, but that coarse grained statistics like mass accretion rates are almost identical to the cold dark matter case.
the mass function and progenitors of halos are strongly suppressed below the warm dark matter free streaming length.

the mass accreted onto a halo is almost indistinguishable in cold and warm dark matters cases, but that the mass functions and progenitor mass function are significantly different, and that the correct solution for first crossing distribution in excursion set theory is crucial for the correct description of the halo mass and subhalo mass functions in warm dark matter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the properties of dark matter particles affect the evolution of the large-scale structure of the Universe and the formation of the galaxies within it.
the development of a robust methodology to study dark matter halo merger histories in non cold dark material models.
the formation and evolution of dark matter structures in the universe.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
warm dark matter haloes are less abundant, but otherwise very similar to their cold dark matter counterparts.
the halo mass function, merger rates, and merger trees in warm dark matter are very similar to those in cold dark matter once the accreted smoothly distributed matter is included.

the merger history of dark matter haloes in the warm dark matter case is very similar to that of the cold dark matter case, except for the suppression of low mass halos, but that the halo mass function, and the progenitor mass function are significantly affected by the warm dark matter free streaming length, and the halo mass function in particular is strongly suppressed below the warm dark matter particle free streaming scale.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
warm dark matter haloes are less numerous than cold dark matter haloes, but that they have very similar merger histories.
the merger histories of haloes are very similar in the two dark matter models, but the mass function of haloes is very different.

the warm dark matter halo mass function and merger history are well described by the generalized extended Press-Schechter formalism, and that the merger history of haloes is almost indistinguishable from cold dark matter, with the main differences being in the halo mass function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the generalized extended Press-Schechter formalism provides a powerful tool for exploring the properties of the dark matter subhalo population in non cold dark mater universes.

a wide variety of halo mass functions, merger histories and merger trees can be rapidly computed for a wide range of models, including those with non standard power spectra, and that the results are accurate to the level of current N body simulations.
the merger history of a halo is a robust observable that can be used to distinguish between dark matter models.
